searches.reason: Replace single-negative training margins with a diagnostic of ranking failure under realistic competition. Seek bounded, paired probes comparing BCE-1, BCE-32 and softmax-32 on identical training prefixes and candidate pools, reporting positive rank, hard-negative concentration and gradient allocation to item embeddings versus the sequence encoder. Separate score-scale changes from ranking changes; use training-only popularity strata. Keep the pinned host validation unchanged and distinguish auxiliary full-catalog diagnostics from benchmark HR@10.

searches.reason: Turn qualitative complaints about redundant alternatives, incompatible products and broad associations into auditable recommendation-level evidence. Seek methods using only public histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions, with cited text spans and explicit unknown outcomes when requirements or intent lack evidence. Start with the required twenty users’ full-catalog unseen-item recommendations; calibrate evidence coding against available feedback without treating simulator judgments as observed preferences or using unavailable reviews, attributes or pretrained weights.

searches.reason: Develop a controlled intervention suite that tests whether diagnoses identify specific failure mechanisms. Compare removal of recent, repeated and distant events with matched random deletions, and order changes that preserve item counts, while controlling padding and position shifts. Validate probe behavior using popularity-only, last-item and order-insensitive controls plus score-rescaling invariance checks. These feasible early experiments can distinguish history sensitivity from evidence of useful sequence modeling; inference perturbations alone do not establish causal user intent.
